status: WRITTEN candidates with WRITTEN-checked-in-kernel explicit examples; not parent adoption
finding: A different genuine root-geometry obstruction: the full-width strictly stable septic interval box centered at (s+1)*((s+1/100)^2+1)^3 with coefficient radius 1/500000 has the center as a common numerator, yet EVERY common numerator must contain at least two nonreal conjugate root pairs. Stronger, at least two upper-half-plane numerator roots, counted with multiplicity, lie within 197/500 of i[9/10,11/10], with conjugates near the reflected segment. These are literal numerator roots even if cancellation occurs. Exact 28 Hurwitz minors, 296 pairing Bernstein coefficients and rational phase/localization comparisons were independently replayed.
general_result: For every degree n>=4 there is an explicit full-width robustly stable interval box with a common numerator but requiring at least floor(n/2)-1 nonreal conjugate pairs in every common numerator. Two cross-member phase inequalities give general sufficient certificates for root-count and root-localization lower bounds, without assuming interval structure.
genuinely_collective_example: On another full-width robustly stable septic box, a two-ACTUAL-corner phase inequality at frequencies 14 and 25 proves no all-real-rooted common numerator, while none of the four individual corners satisfies the same criterion at those same frequencies. This persists on a full 14-endpoint neighborhood and a fixed unrestricted common numerator works. Exact phase comparisons use rational Machin/atan/log intervals and Sturm quadrant counts, not floats.
remaining_gap: All examples have a known unrestricted common numerator. Root-count/localization restrictions do not exclude all numerators; no actual stable septic counterexample and no universal positive theorem are established.
next_action: Investigate whether incompatible root-localization demands from distinct actual members can force more than three conjugate pairs on a single stable septic box, or prove such demands are obstructed by interval stability.
